summary: Ridge lookout in Kananaskis Country that succeeded the Cameron lookout on Mount Burke; the present building dates to 1977 and sits behind a locked fence.

facts.design: Cabin (register type); present building dates to 1977

access.note: Friends of Kananaskis Country describe a workplace and private residence behind a locked, gated barbed wire fence. The register lists access by air. No source describes public visits.

events.note: Cameron lookout on Mount Burke decommissioned; a road was built to the top of Raspberry Ridge.
A new 12 ft by 12 ft lookout was staffed for the first time.
The present building replaced the 1954 lookout; the register gives 1977 as its construction year.
Access road reclaimed; helicopters had made it unnecessary from the 1980s.

evidence.quote: Raspberry Ridge is the second of the lookouts in that “forgotten corner” of K-Country.

evidence.supports: Raspberry replaced the Cameron lookout on Mount Burke, decommissioned 1953
evidence.quote: Raspberry replaced the Cameron lookout on Mt. Burke when that lookout was decommissioned in 1953.

evidence.supports: reason for the move is unclear; most believe no road could reach the top of Mount Burke
evidence.quote: While the reasons for the relocation aren’t really clear, most believe it was because you couldn’t build a road to the top of Mt. Burke.

evidence.supports: road built to the ridge in 1953
evidence.quote: Accordingly, in 1953, a road was constructed to the top of Raspberry Ridge.

evidence.supports: 12 ft by 12 ft lookout first staffed in 1954
evidence.quote: A new, standard 12’ x 12’ lookout was constructed, and staffed for the first time in 1954.

evidence.supports: present building replaced the 1954 lookout in 1977
evidence.quote: It was replaced by the present building in 1977.

evidence.supports: register: cabin type, built 1977, 2 m tall, 2,360 m elevation, active, access by air
access road no longer needed from the 1980s because of helicopters
evidence.quote: Courtesy of helicopters, the access road ceased being necessary in the 1980’s.

evidence.supports: FireNet radio repeater station on the ridge
evidence.quote: In addition to the lookout, there’s also a FireNet radio repeater station up there.

evidence.supports: workplace and private place of residence
evidence.quote: As usual with fire lookouts, remember that this is both a workplace and private place of residence.

evidence.supports: locked, gated barbed wire fence about 100 m back from the lookout
evidence.quote: This one in particular is surrounded by a locked, gated barbed wire fence about 100 m back from the lookout itself

evidence.supports: each lookout site is staffed by an observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 1977 date is for the present cabin. The Friends account dates the first lookout here to 1954 and says the present building replaced it in 1977. The two sources agree.

notes_for_editor: The 1953 road, the 1954 first staffing and the Cameron replacement come only from Friends of Kananaskis Country, a volunteer group; the register's 1977 date matches it. The register's 'Cabin' type and 2 m height describe the present building; no source gives a tower height. The brief's access 'closed' and its boilerplate note ('staffed March-October', 'please don't visit uninvited') appear in no source read; access is recorded as private from the Friends' 'private place of residence' and the locked fence. Staffing as_of 2026 reflects the register's active flag in the snapshot read on 2026-10-20; Alberta.ca says generally April to October. The brief's 'ground' kind is kept; the register calls it a Cabin. No photos saved. The route and trail details on the Friends page are left out on purpose.
